scenes.title: Define your exploration boundary
scenes.visual: Founder reviews anonymous customer and problem cards.
scenes.narration: A market landscape helps you understand the approaches around a customer task. Start with the group, job, context and geography you are exploring. These are working boundaries, not a proven market. A broad industry headline is not automatically relevant to your specific problem.

scenes.title: Map the same job
scenes.visual: Editable direct, indirect and status-quo cards.
scenes.narration: Direct alternatives offer a similar approach to the same job. Indirect alternatives use a different approach. The status quo includes manual help, existing habits and doing nothing. In a fictional registration example, directions, staff help and existing information may all matter. Do not assume a new app is necessary.

scenes.title: Describe without inventing
scenes.visual: Founder records a dated document reference.
scenes.narration: For each approach, record whom it serves, how it helps, where it is available and the source and date. Unknown availability, pricing and performance stay unknown. A provider’s claim describes what it says; it is not independent evidence of customer outcomes.

scenes.title: Compare fairly
scenes.narration: Use the same criteria for the same task and context. Include benefits as well as limits. Avoid declaring a winner or inventing weakness to make your idea look better. An incomplete search does not prove there are no competitors, and repeated reports may share one source.

scenes.title: Treat gaps as hypotheses
scenes.visual: Editable possible gap and verification question cards.
scenes.narration: An apparent gap may reflect incomplete research, a small need, access barriers or a good existing workaround. Record it as a hypothesis with a check. Do not turn a large industry number into your reachable market or claim demand from a few examples. Market sizing comes with its own definitions and evidence.

scenes.title: Build the landscape map
scenes.narration: Create your Market Landscape Map: boundaries, current approach, two other approaches or options still to find, common comparison criteria, evidence limits, a possible gap and a next research check. Keep the map revisable. Next you will combine your learning into a discovery research plan.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Understand the landscape around one job.

children: A
market boundary
defines the group, task, context and geography you will investigate. A
direct alternative
uses a similar approach for the same job; an
indirect alternative
uses another route. The
status quo
includes current behaviour, manual help and doing nothing. These labels depend on the job and approach you have defined.
Illustrative example:

a first-time visitor wants to find registration at a venue. Signs, staff help and existing digital information can serve that job. Their actual availability and usefulness remain to be checked. This is not a review of real providers.
Build a fair map
Define who, job, setting, geography and exclusions.
Start with the current approach; search beyond similar apps.
Record two other approaches or honest options still to find.
Use the same criteria and source/date labels.
Keep claims, verified facts and unknowns separate.
Describe a possible gap as a hypothesis with a check.

A provider’s website supports what it describes, not necessarily actual customer outcomes. Unknown prices or availability are not zero. No search is exhaustive; “not yet found” is different from “does not exist.”
Market numbers need their own evidence
A global industry figure is not your reachable customer market. Do not invent market size, share or demand here. Record scope, date, definition and source if you investigate a number later.

Simulated Coach · no AI connection
Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.

replies.teach: Define the customer job and boundaries. Include direct/indirect alternatives and the status quo; compare benefits and limits fairly.
replies.guide: Map current behaviour and two other approaches or honest search plans. Preserve source/date/status, search limits and a gap hypothesis with a check.
replies.review: Landscape Map check: {missing} required fields still empty. This scripted check counts fields only; it cannot verify competitors, market size, source claims or demand.
replies.challenge: Is the gap only incomplete research? What works well already? Are provider claims verified? Does an industry number actually match your scope?
